title: Four comforts
hookLine: whether or not there is another world, a kind and clean heart is safe (AN 3.65)
carry: one kind act, one clean choice

lines: A PEACE THAT DOESN'T NEED THE ANSWER.
cards: After the questions, the Kalamas have agreed that greed, hatred and confusion lead to harm. But one question still hangs in the air, the one the traveling teachers argued about most. What happens after death?
Is there another world? Do our deeds bear fruit? Every teacher who came through town had a different answer, and the Kalamas couldn't check any of them.
The Buddha doesn't settle the argument. Instead, he describes a person who doesn't need it settled to be at peace.

teach.h: A HEART FREE OF GREED AND ILL WILL
teach.b: At the end of AN 3.65, the Buddha describes a noble disciple whose heart is free of greed and ill will, unconfused, mindful.
Someone who fills the world in every direction with kindness, compassion, gladness for others, and calm. That person, he says, has four comforts here and now.

teach.h: IF THERE IS ANOTHER WORLD, OR IF NOT
teach.b: Paraphrased: first, if there is another world, and good and bad deeds bear fruit, then after death I'll arise somewhere good.
Second, if there is no other world, and deeds bear no fruit, then here, in this very life, I live free of hostility and trouble, at ease.

teach.h: IF EVIL RETURNS, OR IF NOT
teach.b: Third, if evil comes to those who do evil, well, I intend evil toward no one. How could suffering touch me, who do no evil? Fourth, if evil doesn't come to those who do evil, then either way I see myself as clean.

Each comfort has an if. Speaking to people who don't yet accept his teaching, the Buddha doesn't ask them to take rebirth or karma on faith. He shows that a kind and clean heart comes out well on every branch.
Elsewhere, he teaches rebirth and karma plainly, and Buddhist traditions hold them as central.

teach.h: MEETING THE KALAMAS WHERE THEY ARE
teach.b: Here, he meets the Kalamas where they are. The Kalamas, the sutta says, were delighted, and went for refuge.
Look back at this week: the fire sermon, read whole, the eye as an ocean, a king hunting the sound inside a lute, the Numbered Sayings, the luminous mind, know for yourselves.
And now four comforts, for anyone, whatever they believe.

how: Many Buddhists practice the four immeasurables, kindness, compassion, gladness and equanimity, radiating them in every direction, a practice the end of the Kalama Sutta describes.

o: four rules for living a quiet life
four rewards promised in the next life
four assurances for a kind, clean heart

p: I live at ease here and now
I intend evil to no one
I see myself clean either way

s: the four comforts ask the Kalamas to accept rebirth first
each comfort begins with an if: a kind heart comes out well either way.
the disciple in the passage fills every direction with kindness
with kindness, compassion, gladness and calm.
the Buddha never teaches rebirth or karma elsewhere
he teaches them plainly elsewhere; here he meets the Kalamas where they are.

games.q: the Kalamas can't check what happens after death. every teacher says something different. what does the Buddha offer them?
o: a proof that there is another world.
four comforts: a kind, clean heart is safe either way.
games.why: he doesn't settle the argument. he shows that the one with a kind heart is at ease on every branch of it.

practice: Bring to mind someone you love, and let a simple wish for their well-being warm the chest.
Then widen it, to people in this building, this street, this city, in every direction, the way the sutta pictures kindness filling the world, without forcing the feeling.
Rest inside that circle, and notice: right now, with a kind heart, nothing needs settling.

wordCard.voice: Four comforts. In AN 3.65, the one with a kind, clean heart is at ease whether or not there is another world, and whether or not deeds bear fruit. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali assasa: comfort, solace, assurance; the four assasa of AN 3.65.

carryVoice: Your line: one kind act, one clean choice. A kind heart comes out well on every branch. That's the week.
